en: I praise the Lord, the Master of life, the All-pervading One, the Lord of the universe, the Lord of the lords of the world, who partakes in eternal bliss;
the Sovereign of the past, present, and future, the Lord of beings, Śiva, Śaṅkara, Śambhu, and Īśāna. 1.

I praise Śiva, the benefactor, Śambhu, the Sovereign, who wears a garland of skulls around his neck, a mass of serpents upon his body, and who is the Great Time (Mahākāla) and Death (Kāla); who is the protector of Gaṇeśa and the other attendants; and who is vast with the surging waves of the Gaṅgā in his matted locks. 2.

I praise Śiva, the benefactor, Śambhu, the Sovereign Lord—the mine of joy, the ornament who adorns the great Maṇḍala, the wearer of the ashes as his decoration, the beginningless and boundless destroyer of the great delusion. 3.
I praise the one who dwells beneath the banyan tree, whose great laughter is loud, who destroys great sin, and who is ever brilliantly manifest;
I praise Girīśa, Gaṇeśa, Sureśa, Maheśa, Śiva, Śaṅkara, Śambhu, and Īśāna. (4)

I praise Śiva, the benefactor, Śambhu, the Sovereign, who is praised by Brahmā and the other gods as the Supreme Brahman; he who always dwells upon the mountain with half of his body embraced by the Daughter of the Mountain King, and whose abode is the mountain itself. 5.

I praise Śiva, the benefactor, Śambhu, the Sovereign Lord, the foremost among the gods, who holds a skull and a trident in his two hands, who grants all desires to those who bow at his lotus feet, and who is as powerful as a bull. 6.

I praise Śiva, the benefactor, Śambhu, the Sovereign Lord—whose body is like the autumn moon, who is the vessel of joy for his attendants, the three-eyed, the pure, the friend of the Lord of Wealth, whose consort is Aparṇā, and whose conduct is ever virtuous. (7)

I praise Hara, who wears a serpent as a necklace, who sports upon the ground of the funeral pyre, who is Bhava, the essence of the Vedas, eternally changeless, dwelling in the cremation ground, burning with passion yet auspicious, the benefactor Śambhu, the Sovereign Lord Īśāna. (8)

The man who himself recites this Jewel of a Hymn at dawn, having obtained the jewels found here—having propitiated them with excellent sons, abundant grain, virtuous friends, and a wonderful wife—he attains liberation. (9)
